brief.headline: Tech leads a neutral tape; gold rolls over and energy stays heavy
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 0.97% above its 50-day and 7.3% above its 200-day, essentially flat on the week (minus 0.2%). VIX at 16.13 is just above its 20-day average of 15.96, signaling no fear spike but no complacency either. Breadth is the red flag: only 2 of 11 sectors are above their 50-day moving averages, with XLK the lone positive sector-momentum reading at plus 7.6% over 20 days. Every other sector is negative. This is a narrow rally, not a healthy one. Treat breakouts in lagging sectors with extra skepticism until breadth improves.

portfolio.note: Price at $517.53, up 3.2% above 20-DMA, RSI 62.7, bullish MA stack intact. Earnings on Oct 28 are the next event; EPS growth estimate is 14.3% with nearly flat revisions, so no catalyst to reframe the thesis yet.

Up 7.1% on the week to $1,867, just 0.3% off its 20-day high, trailing P/E 60.6x versus a historical median of 39.3x (54% premium). Earnings land Oct 14, nine days out; any miss on bookings guidance at this valuation will hit hard.

XLE at $62.82 is 0.7% below its 20-DMA with 20-day momentum of minus 2.2%, and the energy sector is the second-worst performer over 20 days. Cost basis is $88 against a current price of $62.82, a 28.6% unrealized loss; worth deciding before crude rolls further.

GLD dropped 3.4% this week to $380.14, now 3.3% below its 20-DMA, 5.3% below its 40-DMA, RSI 38.8 and 6.8% off the 20-day high. The gold futures momentum over 20 days is minus 6.5%. The trend has flipped bearish across all short-to-medium timeframes and the thesis needs revisiting.

watchlist.name: Advanced Micro Devices
watchlist.thesis: AMD is 11.9% above its 20-DMA and 24.2% above its 100-DMA, with 20-day momentum of plus 39%. RSI at 70.1 is just touching overbought. EPS estimates revised up by 3 analysts in 30 days, forward P/E 40.6x versus a historical median of 100.8x, so earnings multiples actually look undemanding. Earnings are Nov 3, giving the setup a five-week runway.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: $566.49. 20-day high: $645.46. ATR-based stop distance: ~2.4x ATR (~$58, or roughly $576)
watchlist.risk: RSI at 70 and high 20-day vol of 54% mean any sector rotation out of tech could produce a sharp drawdown quickly.

watchlist.name: Micron Technology
watchlist.thesis: MU has the strongest estimate revision in the screen: EPS revised up 140% and revenue up 112% over 30 days, with 5 analysts raising versus 1 cutting. Trailing P/E is only 14.5x, forward P/E 5.2x. Price is 4.9% above its 20-DMA with RSI 59, not yet extended. Earnings not until Dec 23.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: $1,025. 20-day high: $1,108.72. ATR-based stop distance: ~$46 (one ATR below 20-DMA, ~$979)
watchlist.risk: High volatility (20-day realized vol 50.8%); a broader risk-off move or semiconductor sector reversal would drag MU down fast despite strong fundamentals.

watchlist.name: CrowdStrike
watchlist.thesis: CRWD is 11.5% above its 20-DMA and 36.1% above its 100-DMA, up 7.1% on the week. 20-day market RS is plus 25.8%. The setup is extended but momentum is genuine in the only sector working right now. Earnings Dec 1 keep event risk manageable.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~$242.20 (implied). 20-day high: ~$273.54 (implied from minus 1.3% off high). ATR-based stop distance: ~$11.4 (one ATR)
watchlist.risk: Trailing P/E of 4,501x means price is entirely sentiment-driven; any macro risk-off or sector rotation crushes it without a fundamental floor.

watchlist.name: Intel
watchlist.thesis: INTC is up 30% over 20 days and 16% over 40 days, but sits 6.4% off its 20-day high with a mixed DMA stack and earnings on Oct 22. CY EPS growth estimate is plus 262% off a depressed base, yet revisions are flat at zero. The move may be repositioning ahead of earnings rather than fundamental confirmation.
watchlist.risk: Flat estimate revisions and zero earnings-revision activity mean the Oct 22 print is binary; the 74% realized vol amplifies both directions.

watchlist.name: Novo Nordisk
watchlist.thesis: NVO is in a full bear stack: 9.2% below its 20-DMA, 17.3% below its 100-DMA, RSI 27.1, and 20.2% off its 20-day high. EPS estimates cut by 2.2% in 30 days, with CY growth now slightly negative. The stock's trailing P/E of 9.1x sits at a 224% premium to its own historical median of 2.8x, suggesting the historical anchor is unreliable. The downtrend has lasted 40+ days.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: $41.10. 20-day high: $46.74. ATR-based stop distance: ~$1.07 per ATR
watchlist.risk: RSI at 27 is technically oversold; any pipeline news or sector rotation into defensives could produce a sharp short-covering bounce.

watchlist.name: Adobe
watchlist.thesis: ADBE is 3.8% below its 20-DMA, 8.8% below its 40-DMA, and 13.9% off its 20-day high. 20-day momentum is minus 16.8% and sector RS is minus 24.4%, the worst in the screen. Trailing P/E 13.3x is 56% cheap versus history, but cheap does not stop a falling knife in a narrow tape that already disfavors software.
watchlist.risk: Earnings Dec 9 are far out; a relief bounce is possible on any sector rotation back to software, especially given the low RSI of 41.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold futures at $4,185 are 3.1% below the 20-DMA and 6.8% off the 20-day high, with RSI 36.9 and 20-day momentum of minus 6.5%. The move lower is broad-based across timeframes; watch whether $4,100 provides any support.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: WTI at $90.14 dropped 2.7% on the week and sits 6.1% below its 20-DMA, now 15.6% off the 20-day high despite a still-bullish 100-DMA stack. RSI 45.8 is neutral; the 20-day momentum has flipped to minus 1.5% while the 40-day holds at plus 15.3%, signaling a short-term correction within a medium-term uptrend.

commodities.name: Brent Crude
commodities.note: Brent at $102.53 holds better than WTI, only 1.1% below its 20-DMA versus WTI's 6.1% gap, with positive 20-day momentum of plus 6.5%. The WTI-Brent spread widening is worth monitoring as a signal of localized supply disruptions.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Nat gas at $3.034 is up 1.1% on the week and 2.3% above its 20-DMA, but remains 8.5% off the 20-day high on thin volume (rel volume 0.25). Momentum is only plus 2% over 20 days; the move is constructive but not yet confirmed.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper at $6.62 is barely above its 20-DMA (plus 0.6%) with flat 20-day momentum of plus 0.4%, though elevated relative volume (5.7x) is notable. Copper is a useful macro read; the neutral momentum suggests no clear growth acceleration or deceleration signal right now.

risks: ASML earnings Oct 14: booking guidance miss at 54% P/E premium to history is a meaningful portfolio risk given the 128% unrealized gain.
INTC earnings Oct 22 and MSFT earnings Oct 28 create consecutive event risk in the only sector with positive tape momentum.
Breadth remains extremely narrow: 10 of 11 sectors below their 50-day averages. Any rotation out of XLK has no backstop from other sectors.
Gold and GLD rolling over simultaneously removes the traditional defensive hedge from the portfolio at a point when breadth is already weak.

WTI crude sitting 15.6% off its 20-day high despite a bullish longer-term stack signals potential demand-side concern; a break below $88 would likely pressure XLE further against an already underwater position.
